author: Rachel Libert
title: Poyer, Phillips making an unexpected impact for Bills - NewsBreak
text:
By Rachel Libert Thad Brown ,
8 hours ago
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. (WROC) – It’s unlikely that anyone thought there would be any playing time for Jordan Poyer or Jordan Phillips this season.
But, there they were against the Chiefs.
Poyer was fourth on the team in tackles with five, and Phillips was the hero on the first-half goal line stand thanks to key pressures on first and second down.
Their mid-30s success has been a mix of humility and confidence.
“Grateful to even be here, talking to you all. I came in here in August, and it was probably one of the best mindsets coming in that I’ve had going into a season,” Poyer said. “I felt, you know, just the idea of coming in like a rookie, training like a rookie. If I was going to play, that would happen. If I wasn’t, I was okay with that as well.”
Poyer’s mindset was a little bit different than his teammate’s.
“If you ask me, I’m the best player in the league,” Phillips said. “My confidence is always going to be there, and it’s nice to see that it still translates on the field.”
The impact of the veterans hasn’t gone unnoticed from the Bills’ coaching staff.
“It’s really kind of surreal to watch, because they’ve been around for a number of years,” Sean McDermott said. “Neither of them are as young as they used to be, and yet, what they’ve brought to our team from an attitude, leadership, energy standpoint has been felt in a very impactful way.”
In his 10th season in the league, Phillips shared how he stays ready as one of the older guys on the field.
“At this point, it’s just making sure you have enough juice in the game,” Phillips said. “Making sure that you work your fundamentals and stuff during the week, but ultimately, making sure that you’re ready to go on Sunday.”
Poyer shared his thoughts on his personal growth so far.
“Two-and-a-half games in, and I still think I can continue to get better,” Poyer said. “And I will get better.”
The duo’s impact isn’t just being felt on game days, but also in the locker room. Rookie Deone Walker said Phillips still brings the joy and intensity just like he did in his younger days.
“No matter if I’m in a bad mood, sad,” Walker said, “He’s still lifting me up.”
